newsitem.title: UK: Barclays to be EMU-ready, even without stg.
newsitem.headline: Barclays to be EMU-ready, even without stg.

text.p: Barclays Plc, one of Britain's largest banks said it will have its wholesale operations ready to deal with a single European currency despite the fact the bank does not believe sterling will join EMU in the first wave in 1999.

"We have continental European operations ourselves, as do many of our corporate customers, or they may trade with the continent," a Barclays spokeswoman told Reuters. "We will ensure we are ready to handle the Euro in wholesale markets and to meet the needs of our customers."
Barclays chairman Andrew Buxton said earlier that Britain should not join EMU in the first wave.
"I think Britain should not join in the first round. There are many reasons for this, but the main reason is that we don't have enough exchange rate stability," Buxton said in a BBC radio interview.

Buxton was echoing the recently expressed views of Barclays chief executive Martin Taylor, who said in March that sterling should not join in the first wave because no-one knows at what rate it should do so, adding that this stemmed principally from the fact that the UK economic cycle is unsynchronised with that of the rest of Europe.
In common with most British banks, Barclays supports the country's continued membership of the European Union but is working on the basis that sterling will not join EMU in the first wave.
This has meant that the large investment to adapt banks' retail operations to the single currency has not yet been entered into although preparations are under way.
On the wholesale side, however, banks have to be ready to deal on January 1, 1999.
"We have already made significant progress in our preparations," the spokeswoman added.
Barclays has prepared a guide for its customers on the implications of EMU and is inviting business customers to a series of seminars on the subject.
